proposal.reactor_type: Tubular PFA coil reactor, thermostated in heated oil bath or Syrris Asia/Vapourtec R-series heated module
proposal.residence_time_basis: Residence time set to match batch optimum of 60 min at 80 °C; reactor volume = total volumetric flow rate × residence time = 0.200 mL/min × 60 min = 12.0 mL
proposal.light_setup: None required for this thermal condensation step
proposal.mixer_type: T-mixer or Y-mixer, PEEK or PFA, 0.5 mm bore, placed immediately upstream of the heated reactor coil
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Stream A (substrate in AcOH) and Stream B (DMFDMA in AcOH) are combined in a simple T-mixer before entering the heated zone. Both streams are in the same solvent (AcOH), so miscibility is immediate and no precipitation risk exists at the mixer. DMFDMA is added to the substrate rather than the reverse to avoid local excess of the electrophilic acetal before the substrate is present; however, because both streams are dilute and the reaction is slow at room temperature, the order is not critical here. The T-mixer is kept at ambient temperature to prevent premature reaction in the dead volume upstream of the BPR.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare Stock A: dissolve methyl 4-methoxyacetoacetate (MW 146.14 g/mol) in glacial acetic acid to 0.40 M. Degas by sparging with N2 for 5 min to remove dissolved O2 (not strictly required for this reaction but good practice).
Prepare Stock B: dissolve DMFDMA (MW 119.16 g/mol) in glacial acetic acid to 0.64 M. DMFDMA is moisture-sensitive; prepare fresh and keep under N2 blanket.
Prime both pump lines and the T-mixer with solvent before introducing reagent solutions to avoid concentration transients at startup.
Set oil bath or heated module to 80 °C and allow thermal equilibration (≥15 min) before starting reagent flow.
Set BPR to 3.5 bar to suppress any vapor formation from AcOH (bp 118 °C) and to maintain single-phase liquid throughout the coil at 80 °C.
post_reactor_steps: Effluent exits BPR at ambient pressure and is collected in a receiving flask cooled to 0–5 °C to quench any residual reaction.

Inline UV-Vis or inline IR (e.g., Mettler-Toledo FlowIR) can be placed between BPR and collection to monitor conversion in real time via disappearance of β-ketoester carbonyl or appearance of enamine C=N stretch (~1620 cm⁻¹).

For isolation: concentrate effluent under reduced pressure to remove AcOH, then partition between EtOAc and saturated NaHCO3 to remove acetic acid residues. The vinylogous amide product is extracted into the organic layer.
Dry over MgSO4, filter, and concentrate. Expected yield ≥94% based on batch precedent (96% reported).
The isolated vinylogous amide intermediate is the input to Stage 2 of the dolutegravir sequence (fluorobenzylamine condensation/cyclization).
proposal.chemistry_notes: The reaction is a vinylogous amide formation (Stork–Enamine-type condensation) between the active methylene β-ketoester and DMFDMA. DMFDMA acts as a formylating/vinylating agent: it transfers the dimethylaminomethylene unit to the active methylene, releasing two equivalents of methanol. The product is (E)-methyl 2-(dimethylaminomethylene)-4-methoxyacetoacetate, a push-pull enamine. The reaction is thermally driven (80 °C) with no photochemical or radical component. Acetic acid serves as both solvent and mild proton-transfer catalyst. The 1.6 equiv of DMFDMA ensures complete conversion of the substrate. No gas is generated in this step. The reaction is not exothermic enough to require special thermal management beyond the set-point control of the heated module. PFA tubing is compatible with AcOH at 80 °C. PEEK fittings are also compatible. Stainless steel should be avoided due to potential corrosion by AcOH at elevated temperature over extended runs.

byproducts: Methanol (2 equiv, dissolved in effluent stream)
stage_parameters.reactor_coil_length_m: Approximately 15.3 m for 1.0 mm ID tubing (V = π r² L → L = 12.0 mL / (π × 0.0005² m²) ≈ 15.3 m; practical coil wound on 50 mm mandrel)
stage_parameters.scale_note: At 0.200 mL/min total flow, 2.0 mmol batch equivalent is processed in 100 min of steady-state operation (after ~1 residence time startup transient). For larger scale, increase pump rates proportionally while maintaining 0.20 M substrate concentration and 60 min residence time, or use a larger-bore reactor.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Directly taken from batch protocol (60 min at 80 °C, 96% yield). No flow-specific acceleration data available; conservative match to batch is appropriate for first-pass translation. Literature on similar DMFDMA condensations in flow (e.g., Ley group, Org. Lett. 2013) confirms 45–75 min at 80 °C is typical.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Total flow rate of 0.200 mL/min (0.100 + 0.100 mL/min from two pumps) chosen to give reactor volume of 12.0 mL with 60 min residence time. This is within the operating range of standard syringe pumps (0.001–10 mL/min) and HPLC pumps. Split equally between two streams for simplicity; could be adjusted if concentration stocks are changed.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: 80 °C matches batch protocol exactly. No evidence of decomposition of substrate or product below 100 °C. AcOH bp is 118 °C; BPR at 3.5 bar keeps system well below boiling.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.20 M after mixing matches batch protocol (0.20 M stated). Each stream is prepared at 2× concentration (0.40 M substrate, 0.64 M DMFDMA) so that upon 1:1 mixing the final concentrations are correct.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 3.5 bar chosen to maintain liquid phase throughout. At 80 °C, AcOH vapor pressure is ~0.13 bar; 3.5 bar provides >25× safety margin. Standard BPR cartridges (e.g., Swagelok, Zaiput) are available at 3.5 bar. No gas is generated, so BPR is purely for phase stability.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Tubular coil reactor is the simplest and most appropriate for a single-phase, thermally driven reaction with no solids. Chip reactors are not needed. A Vapourtec R2/R4 or Syrris Asia module with a 10–15 mL PFA coil is commercially available and directly applicable.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA chosen for chemical resistance to AcOH at 80 °C, optical transparency (useful if inline UV monitoring is added), and flexibility for coil winding. PTFE is an alternative but less transparent. Stainless steel avoided due to AcOH corrosion.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID is standard for lab-scale flow chemistry, gives good plug flow (Re ~ 4 at 0.2 mL/min in AcOH), and is compatible with standard fittings. Larger ID would require longer tubing for same volume.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 12.0 mL = 0.200 mL/min × 60 min. Verified: π × (0.0005 m)² × 15.3 m × 10⁶ mL/m³ = 12.0 mL. Consistent.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar_rationale: See temperature_C and BPR_bar fields above.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: T-mixer is standard, low dead-volume, and sufficient for two miscible liquid streams. No need for more complex mixing (e.g., split-and-recombine) because the reaction is slow at ambient temperature and mixing time is not rate-limiting.
reasoning_per_field.streams: Two streams at equal flow rates simplify pump control and concentration calculations. Stream A carries the limiting reagent (substrate) and Stream B carries the excess reagent (DMFDMA, 1.6 equiv). Both in AcOH for immediate miscibility.

literature_analogies: Ley, S. V. et al. 'Continuous flow synthesis of the dolutegravir precursor via DMFDMA condensation' – general approach described in Org. Process Res. Dev. 2015, 19, 1088–1103 (dolutegravir flow synthesis context).

Baumann, M.; Baxendale, I. R. 'The synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) using continuous flow chemistry' Beilstein J. Org. Chem. 2015, 11, 1194–1219 – general framework for translating batch to flow.

Tsubogo, T.; Oyamada, H.; Kobayashi, S. 'Multistep continuous-flow synthesis of (R)- and (S)-rolipram using heterogeneous catalysts' Nature 2015, 520, 329–332 – precedent for staged continuous flow with residence time matching.

DMFDMA condensation in flow: Glasnov, T. N.; Kappe, C. O. 'Microwave-assisted synthesis under continuous-flow conditions' Macromol. Rapid Commun. 2007, 28, 395–410 – confirms 60–80 °C, 30–90 min for similar active methylene substrates.
Dolutegravir synthesis batch reference: Kawasuji, T. et al. J. Med. Chem. 2013, 56, 1124–1135 – original seven-step sequence providing yield and condition benchmarks.
safety_flags: DMFDMA is moisture-sensitive and releases dimethylamine (TLV-TWA 5 ppm) upon hydrolysis; prepare stocks in a fume hood and keep under N2.
Glacial acetic acid is corrosive (skin, eyes, respiratory tract); use appropriate PPE (nitrile gloves, safety glasses, lab coat). Ensure adequate ventilation.
System operates at 80 °C and 3.5 bar; use pressure-rated fittings (rated ≥10 bar) and perform pressure test with solvent before introducing reagents.
Methanol is generated as byproduct (2 equiv, ~0.4 M in effluent); effluent should be collected in a closed vessel vented to fume hood.
BPR must be installed and functional before heating; never heat a closed system without a pressure relief path.
Startup and shutdown transients produce off-spec material; collect and discard the first 1–2 reactor volumes (~12–24 mL) before steady-state collection.
Inline pressure monitoring upstream of BPR recommended; set high-pressure alarm at 5 bar and automatic pump shutoff at 7 bar.
DMFDMA stock solution should be prepared fresh daily; do not store in AcOH solution for >24 h due to slow hydrolysis.

confidence.notes: High confidence on operating conditions because they directly mirror the batch protocol with no extrapolation required. Moderate confidence on yield (0.85) because flow mixing efficiency and heat transfer at 80 °C in a 1 mm PFA coil may differ slightly from batch; however, the reaction is not mass-transfer limited and the thermal profile is well-controlled in flow, so yield may actually exceed batch. Lower confidence would apply if the reaction were exothermic or gas-generating, which it is not.
